items.prompt: Orthographic top-down architectural plan photograph of a real built film set, taken straight down from high above: camera axis exactly perpendicular to the ground; no wall face, no elevation, no side of any building, wall, hedge or tree trunk is visible; only the ground plane, the top edges of walls and hedges and the tops of trees, furniture and objects are seen. The top of the image is north. Plan of the interior of a tall Art Nouveau courtroom after Alphonse Mucha, built as a real set, 20 metres long and 13 metres wide, seen from directly above with the roof not present so the whole floor is visible. The room fills most of the image as a rectangle with its long axis running left to right; all four walls are continuous thick dark oak wall lines enclosing the room. The left (south) wall line has one wide gap at its centre: the main double doorway. The right (north) wall line has a small narrow gap near its top corner: the officers' door. The top wall line and the bottom wall line are continuous with no gaps. The top (east) and bottom (west) walls are fully present along the room edges, seen only as their top edges and thickness; the floor ends at those wall lines; windows, doors, carved panels and anything mounted on a wall face are not visible from directly above and must not be drawn. The floor is a mosaic of red, black and buff tesserae with cream and gold vine borders and a large circular roundel pattern at the centre. At the right end a raised dais of three steps carries a double throne, seen from above as two tall crimson-cushioned seats side by side facing left; just left of the dais near the top corner, a low oak herald's step. Along the top wall, left of centre-right, a long raised oak jury-box with two tiers of six seats and a ledge with small slates, facing down into the room. Just below-left of the jury-box, a small raised oak witness box with a rail. Exactly in the middle of the floor a table with a large dish of tarts on it. Along the bottom wall, centre-right, a low oak dock enclosure with an iron rail. Along the left wall inside the doorway, a shallow public gallery seen from above as a narrow balcony floor with a curving verdigris cast-iron front. The open floor between is empty. Warm evening light from the high west windows falls in soft coloured patches across the floor from the bottom wall toward the top wall. The set is empty: no people, no animals, no creatures, no text, no labels, no arrows, no symbols, no map legend. A clean, sharp, evenly exposed photographic plan in which every feature named above is clearly readable in its stated position. Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.
